title: 0.1 + 0.2 comes out to 0.30000000000000004

input.description: Any two decimal prices or quantities added directly, e.g. a $0.10 item plus a $0.20 item, or a 10% discount combined with a 20% discount.

what_goes_wrong: The sum prints as 0.30000000000000004 and `0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3` is false, so an equality check on a computed total silently fails.
why: 0.1 and 0.2 have no exact finite binary fraction (only sums of negative powers of two are exact in IEEE-754 double), so each literal is already rounded to the nearest representable double before the addition happens. Adding those two already-rounded values produces a result that is close to but not exactly the double closest to 0.3. This is a property of binary floating point itself (IEEE 754-2019), not a defect in any one language or runtime.
fix: Never compare floating-point money values for equality. Store money as integer minor units (cents) or use a fixed/decimal type (Python's decimal.Decimal, a cents-as-integer scheme in JS) for anything that gets added, subtracted, or compared.

sources.title: Python docs: 15.1. Floating-Point Arithmetic: Issues and Limitations
What Every Computer Scientist Should Know About Floating-Point Arithmetic (Goldberg, hosted by Oracle)

test_cases.note: A money-adding function should never assume their_function(0.1, 0.2) == 0.3 by direct float comparison; it should return an exact minor-unit integer or Decimal instead.
